text:
BERT4Rec already addresses inference alignment by including last-item-only masking alongside random Cloze training; inference appends a reserved mask token. Thus, terminal-mask supervision is an established control, not a novel adaptive policy. Bidirectional reconstruction is valid, but shifted next-item targets can leak through visible inputs. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690). [Recency Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) motivates sampling more task-relevant training targets, noting that random item reconstruction is only weakly aligned with next-item prediction.

Recent related work provides ideas, rather than direct evidence for this benchmark. [Sequential Masked Modeling (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11150) combines sliding windows with penultimate-token masking for session recommendation. [Q-BERT4Rec (December 2025; revised March 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02474) explores span, tail and multi-region masking, but also introduces multimodal semantic representations and quantization; its overall results cannot establish gains from corruption policy alone. [ScaleRec (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596) uses adaptive patch masking to filter redundant interactions, within a different architecture. These searches did not establish a directly matched context-sufficiency masking result.

Practical hypothesis: compare corrected baseline, random-prefix terminal-mask training, and terminal-mask training with modest prefix corruption, keeping one BERT4Rec model/category and compute fixed. For target x_t, construct only [x_1,…,x_{t−1},MASK]; exclude x_t and its suffix from that example. Adapt corruption to visible prefix length while retaining useful context; treat this as an unverified proposal. Preserve left padding and final-mask readout. Select using the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10: supplied 0.5375 is 0.005 below baseline 0.5425, so it does not support improvement.
